transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya S., Carlos R., Priya P. (Redwood) — Eric H., Sasha I., Lena N. (ValenceCloud)
Notes: call recorded; partial auto-transcript; some ASR errors expected

Summary: quick kickoff, go through marketplace checklist, deep-dive on VPC/private deployment model, SSO/KMS details, and agree next steps.

00:00 - 00:18 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then Carlos will walk through the reference-arch draft we've been iterating on.
00:19 - 00:35 Eric (ValenceCloud): Yep hi, Eric here, Sasha and Lena are on, thanks. We're excited to get this in the marketplace.
00:36 - 01:05 Carlos (Redwood): Cool, so the agenda: marketplace listing requirements, reference arch (two flavors: marketplace-managed hosted, and marketplace listing for private/VPC deployments), billing integration, security checklist, and timeline.
01:06 - 01:30 Sasha (ValenceCloud): Quick ask up front — for customers who want private deployments, what's the minimal infra we need to show on the marketplace? like, do we need full AMI or container images?
01:31 - 02:05 Carlos (Redwood): Good question. For ValenceCloud marketplace, there are two common patterns: 1) a hosted integration where Redwood remains the control plane and the listing points to the hosted API, or 2) a private deployment option where the listing includes a reference-arch and deployment artifacts (Terraform module + container images). For private, we recommend a Terraform module plus Helm chart; AMI is optional.
02:06 - 02:25 Lena (ValenceCloud): And about networking — customers mandate VPC peering or private link? Our marketplace supports both but we need to document which one Redwood supports.
02:26 - 03:00 Carlos (Redwood): We support Private (VPC) deployment with VPC peering and with PrivateLink. Our private package also supports on-prem air-gapped installs but that requires additional packaging. We'll include both in the reference arch doc.
03:01 - 03:35 Maya (Redwood): Important to call out: when listing, we need to be explicit about what features are available in each mode — hosted API features (streaming, function calling) vs private (may have limitations on streaming depending on customer infra). Also mention SLA/troubleshooting paths.
03:36 - 04:10 Eric (ValenceCloud): Understood. On the marketplace listing side, we need a short blurb, logos, screenshots, and a technical requirements box. I'll connect you with our marketplace content owner.
04:11 - 05:00 Carlos (Redwood): I'll prepare that. Now on security and compliance: Lena, can you outline the evidence you need? We typically share SOC 2, ISO docs, pen test summaries, and our KMS integration notes.
05:01 - 05:30 Lena (ValenceCloud): SOC2 and ISO are required for the listing. Also we need clear KMS/HSM workflow — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys in the private deployment? And audit logs retention?
05:31 - 06:10 Carlos (Redwood): For private deployments, yes we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted, customers can bring keys via a KMS integration but the keys remain in their cloud. Audit logs: we can ship to customer S3/Blob or to their logging stack; retention is configurable.
06:11 - 06:45 Sasha (ValenceCloud): Any tricky bits around credentials in marketplace provisioning? we need to ensure users don't have to copy secret keys manually.
06:46 - 07:30 Carlos (Redwood): We use an automated onboarding workflow: marketplace purchase triggers a provisioning webhook, and then we kick off an infra template that binds to the customer's account. For private, often we require a short-lived service role or an install script. We'll document both flows.
07:31 - 08:20 Maya (Redwood): On billing — ValenceCloud marketplace supports both usage-based metering and reserved listing. How do you want to present Redwood offerings? We typically have hosted usage pricing and a Dedicated reserved capacity SKU.
08:21 - 09:00 Eric (ValenceCloud): We want both options. Customers like the simplicity of marketplace usage but some enterprise customers need reserved, predictable pricing. We should show both in the listing.
09:01 - 10:00 Carlos (Redwood): OK we'll provide SKU table: hosted per-token and per-embedding rates, and a reserved capacity monthly commit SKU with throughput sizing guidance. We'll add notes about expected latency and recommended capacity for XQPS.
10:01 - 11:30 Sasha (ValenceCloud): For metering and reporting, does Redwood expose detailed usage reports per tenant so the marketplace can reconcile billing?
11:31 - 12:15 Carlos (Redwood): Yes, we emit per-tenant metering with granular granularity — per-route token counts and per-embedding units. We can provide an S3 export or integrate via the marketplace metering APIs.
12:16 - 13:00 Lena (ValenceCloud): Security again — SSO: SAML is required for some customers; any support for SCIM provisioning and RBAC?
13:01 - 13:45 Priya (Redwood): We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning users; RBAC with role tiers is available in both hosted and private. We'll include sample SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the reference doc.
13:46 - 15:00 Eric (ValenceCloud): Great. On the reference architecture, can we walk through the diagram you shared? (Carlos shares screen)
15:01 - 16:30 Carlos (Redwood): Alright, top-left is marketplace control plane; the center is Redwood runtime which can be deployed either as hosted (in Redwood infra) or as private in-customer VPC. Key components: model runtime (GPU pools), request router, KV cache, and compilation/orchestration layer. For marketplace private listing, the artifacts include a Terraform module that deploys an autoscaling pool, a load balancer, and the Redwood runtime helm chart.
16:31 - 17:20 Sasha (ValenceCloud): For the runtime container, what's the expected image size and GPU driver requirements? We need to put that into the package constraints for the marketplace.
17:21 - 18:00 Carlos (Redwood): Image size: ~1.4GB compressed for the runtime container; requires CUDA 12.x drivers for GPU instances; we support NVIDIA A10/A100 families. We'll list exact drivers and recommended instance types.
18:01 - 19:00 Lena (ValenceCloud): Patching cadence — do you push runtime updates automatically or is it manual for private installs?
19:01 - 20:00 Carlos (Redwood): For private, updates are opt-in: we provide image updates and an upgrade playbook. Customers can schedule rolling upgrades. For hosted, we handle updates with optional maintenance windows.
20:01 - 21:00 Maya (Redwood): Let's talk about model routing and fallback: ValenceCloud needs to know how we handle capacity constraints — do we fall back to smaller model variants or to hosted when private is constrained?
21:01 - 22:00 Carlos (Redwood): We can configure smart routing policies: e.g., route to private first, then fallback to Redwood hosted equivalent model variant in the same region; or throttle/queue based on SLOs. We'll document supported fallback policies in the listing.
22:01 - 24:00 Sasha (ValenceCloud): There's also latency awareness — for callouts that require <200ms, customers may need dedicated capacity. We should recommend that in the docs.
24:01 - 25:00 Priya (Redwood): We'll add a table mapping use-cases to recommended deployment modes (hosted for non-sensitive, private for regulated/low-latency).
25:01 - 27:00 Eric (ValenceCloud): Marketplace listing also needs legal attachments — terms of use, SOC2 attestations, and indemnity language. Who on Redwood can own that?
27:01 - 28:00 Maya (Redwood): Priya will coordinate legal artifacts with our legal ops; I'll copy the right person on follow-ups.
28:01 - 30:00 Lena (ValenceCloud): One security nit: audit log format — can we standardize to CloudTrail-style JSON events so it's easy to ingest?
30:01 - 30:45 Carlos (Redwood): Yes we can emit CloudTrail-compatible events for key actions (auth, model inference, admin changes). We'll include sample event schema.
30:46 - 33:00 Sasha (ValenceCloud): Onboarding flow: can we do a demo of the provisioning webhook and how the marketplace would trigger provisioning? We want to run that in the workshop.
33:01 - 34:00 Carlos (Redwood): Absolutely, workshop will include an end-to-end provisioning demo with a sandbox account.
34:01 - 36:00 Eric (ValenceCloud): About timelines — our marketplace window for new listings next month closes 2026-04-10. If we want to make that cutoff we need final assets by 2026-04-05. Is that realistic?
36:01 - 37:30 Maya (Redwood): Tight, but doable if both teams prioritize. We'll aim to have drafts earlier: Carlos to send ref-arch + sample artifacts by 2026-03-28; ValenceCloud to provide listing contact and terraform by 2026-03-30; then finalize assets first week of April.
37:31 - 39:00 Priya (Redwood): Also we'll need a joint PR/marketing blurb; marketing usually wants 2 weeks to prep. We'll add that to the timeline.
39:01 - 40:00 Eric (ValenceCloud): Competitor notes: some customers evaluate MegaCloud AI marketplace; we should highlight performance and cost benefits in the listing.
40:01 - 42:00 Carlos (Redwood): We'll include a short benchmark excerpt that compares latency / cost per 1k tokens for a typical config — note this is illustrative and not a guarantee.
42:01 - 44:00 Maya (Redwood): One more operational note: support routing — for marketplace purchases, what is the escalation path? We need an on-call contact for initial integration issues.
44:01 - 45:00 Carlos (Redwood): We'll provide a support playbook and an email/Slack channel for partner escalations; for Dedicated/reserved customers we provide a higher SLA and a named CSM.
45:01 - 47:00 Lena (ValenceCloud): Are there any data residency constraints we can't support? We have EU-only customers requiring data to stay in EU for inference.
47:01 - 48:00 Carlos (Redwood): For hosted, we support EU regions via our cloud presence; for private deployments you can pin the deployment to EU-only infra. We'll document region coverage.
48:01 - 50:00 Sasha (ValenceCloud): A quick note on metrics we need during the validation workshop: throughput at 1k QPS, cold start latency, tail latency p99. We'll record those.
50:01 - 51:30 Carlos (Redwood): Good, we'll prepare a benchmark harness and a script to run load tests in the sandbox; will share results after the workshop.
51:31 - 52:30 Maya (Redwood): Recap next steps and owners — Carlos shares ref-arch by 03/28; ValenceCloud sends terraform & listing contact by 03/30; Lena shares KMS constraints by 03/26; Maya schedules the workshop.
52:31 - 53:30 Eric (ValenceCloud): Sounds good. Anything else?
53:31 - 54:50 Priya (Redwood): I'll follow up with a one-pager and a checklist. Thanks everyone.
54:51 - 55:00 Maya (Redwood): Thanks, bye.
